Order Sheet 06.02.2025
Heard Mr. Lukesh Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioners through video conferencing.
Also heard Mr. Hariom Rai, learned Panel Lawyer, appearing for respondent No.1/State and perused the FIR as well as material brought on record.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that there is a matrimonial dispute between petitioner No.1 / husband and respondent No. 2 / wife and marriage between them was solemnized on 15.11.2018 and the present FIR has been lodged by respondent No. 2 against the petitioner for harassment on 21.11.2023.

He further submits that from the perusal of the charge-sheet it is apparent that no prima facie case against the petitioners appears from the allegations levelled therein and the present complaint has been lodged with ill motive to wreak personal vengeance upon the petitioners.

From the perusal of the written complaint also, it is apparent that no specific demand or coercion has been alleged by the complainant and the entire complaint is based on vague grounds and omnibus allegations.

The complainant having concealed in her complaint the fact that despite the financial conditions of her in-laws she was allowed to study law and that too from Raipur which is at a distance of an almost 2 hour journey, despite a law college being there within 20 kms from their house, shows that the complaint lodged by her is drafted after much deliberation and specifically fabricated so as to make out a false cognizable case against the petitioners.
The complainant put forth the actual truth in her complaint, no offence would have been made out and in fact her own fault of illogical and inhumane demands would have been highlighted.
He lastly submits that the present matter be referred to Mediation & Conciliation Centre of this Court being matrimonial in nature as there may be chances of compromise between the parties.

Considering the fact that the dispute arrived between the parties i.e. petitioner No.1 / husband and respondent No. 2 / wife is matrimonial in nature, we deem it appropriate to make an effort to get the said dispute settled by way of mediation.

In view of the above, petitioner No.1 shall deposit Rs. 50,000/- with the Mediation Centre of this Court within a period of two weeks from today and the same shall be paid to respondent No. 2 on her appearance before the Mediation Centre.

The matter is remitted to the Mediation Centre with the direction that the Mediation Centre shall conclude the mediation and conciliation proceedings expeditiously, preferably within a period of two months after giving notices to both the parties.
Parties are directed to appear before the Mediation Centre of this Court on 19.02.2025.

Learned State counsel is directed to inform the private respondent No.2 about passing of this order,
so that she may appear before the Mediation Centre of the aforesaid date.

sentences.text: List this matter along with report of Mediation Centre before this Court on 06.03.2025.

Till the next date of listing, further proceedings in relation to Criminal Case No. 8492/2024,
pending before the learned JMFC, Raipur (C.G.) arising out of the Crime No. 30/2024 registered against the petitioners in Mahila Thana, Raipur (C.G.) for offences under Section 498A, 506, 34 of the IPC, shall remain stayed.
After depositing the amount as aforesaid, notice shall be issued to the parties.

It is made clear that in case the aforesaid amount is not deposited within the aforesaid period, the interim protection granted as above shall automatically be vacated and this petition shall stand dismissed without further reference to any Bench of this Court.

The petitioners are directed to produce the copy of the receipt before the trial Court concerned regarding payment of the said money before the Mediation Centre of this Court in pursuance of this Court's order, then only this order shall be given into effect.
It is also made clear that if any final settlement is arrived at between the parties, the aforesaid amount so deposited, shall be adjusted.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Ravindra Kumar Agrawal) (Ramesh Sinha)
